pr_title: apps/{req,x509,ca}.c Make sure certs have SKID and AKID  by default
pr_body:
This implements the solution for adding by default SKID and AKID X.509 extensions when generating certificates
for compliance with RFC 5280 requirements discussed in #13603:

Make the following X.509 extension configuration options the default for the `ca`, `req`, and `x509` apps:
```
subjectKeyIdentifier=hash
authorityKeyIdentifier=keyid
```
and provide for both of them the possibility to provide instead the value `none` for disabling (default) generation, i.e.,
```
subjectKeyIdentifier=none
authorityKeyIdentifier=none
```

Fixes #13603.

This also
* adds the `-copy_extensions` option to the `req` app, partly fixing #13708
* in `crypto/x509` renames `v3_{skey,skid}.c`, `v3_{akey,akid}.c`, `v3_{alt,san}.c`
* adds check in `Configure` for non-existing source files referred to in `build.info`, 
which may happen for instance after renaming source files.

issue_context.title: Generated X.509 certs should be RFC 5280 compliant by default
issue_context.body:
Meanwhile we have stronger checks for X.509 certificates to comply to RFC 5280, 
at least when strict checking is enabled (e.g., using `-x509_strict`).

Yet unfortunately the OpenSSL apps by default tend to generate certs that are not compliant.
In particular, X.509v3 certs (i.e., those having any X.509 extensions) MUST include 
*  an authority key identifier (AKID) with the exception of self-signed certs - see https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.1
* a subject key identifier (SKID) with the exception of non-CA certs - see https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5280#section-4.2.1.2
comments: I suppose this is something in between bug and feature so I do not expect we will fix this in 1.1.1.
This is something that would be nice to get fixed for 3.0 however it is IMO not a blocker for 3.0 either.

Regarding non-CA certs, the subject key identifier (SKID) is still listed as a SHOULD in RFC 5280:

>    For end entity certificates, the subject key identifier extension
>    provides a means for identifying certificates containing the
>    particular public key used in an application.  Where an end entity
>    has obtained multiple certificates, especially from multiple CAs, the
>    subject key identifier provides a means to quickly identify the set
>    of certificates containing a particular public key.  To assist
>    applications in identifying the appropriate end entity certificate,
>    this extension SHOULD be included in all end entity certificates.

So, while not mandatory, we might want OpenSSL apps generating end-entity certs to include a SKID by default (along with an AKID if they are not self-signed).
The strict cert checking should be fixed to warn about SKID, as in the quote above from RFC 5280.  Want me to open a separate issue?

> The strict cert checking should be fixed to warn about SKID, as in the quote above from RFC 5280. Want me to open a separate issue?

I support this, though AFAIK in libcrypto so far we don't really have a concept of warnings, though would be nice to have.
What the strict cert checking (if enabled) does in case of non-compliance is to throw an error and fail.
Well the SKID is not a MUST, it's a SHOULD so throwing an error when it's missing is wrong.

> Well the SKID is not a MUST, it's a SHOULD so throwing an error when it's missing is wrong.

Sure, and that's why it will be hard to do at lib level.

I'm currently investigating ways of adding default AKIDs and SKIDs to solve the primary topic of this issue.
This should be done at app (not: libcrypto) level, right?

My plan is to do that in `do_X509_sign()` of `req.c`, which is used also by `x509.c` and `ca.c`, as follows:
Just before actually signing the cert template, check if an AKID and/or SKID is missing, and add it if so.
Does anyone have a better suggestion?
Your plan makes sense.  But I think you should add  a config option to make it *not* happen.  A common use of openssl is to generate test certs.

This brings me to a refinement of my plan:

Make the following X.509 extension configuration options the default:
```
subjectKeyIdentifier=hash
authorityKeyIdentifier=keyid
```
and provide for both of them the possibility to provide instead the value `no` for disabling (default) generation, i.e.,
```
subjectKeyIdentifier=no
authorityKeyIdentifier=no
```
Isn't it possible to specify empty value as in `subjectKeyIdentifier=` already? (I did not test that.)

An empty value for SKID and AKID is currently not supported - for instance,
```
apps/openssl req -new -x509 -key fd.key -out fd.crt -subj "/CN=fd" -addext subjectKeyIdentifier=hash -addext authorityKeyIdentifier=
```
yields
```
Error Loading command line extensions
C0E73C60D87F0000:error:1100006C:X509 V3 routines:(unknown function):invalid empty name:crypto/x509/v3_utl.c:360:
C0E73C60D87F0000:error:11000069:X509 V3 routines:(unknown function):invalid extension string:crypto/x509/v3_conf.c:102:name=authorityKeyIdentifier,section=
C0E73C60D87F0000:error:11000080:X509 V3 routines:(unknown function):error in extension:crypto/x509/v3_conf.c:48:section=default, name=authorityKeyIdentifier, value=
```

Using an empty string rather than `no` to indicate forbidding the default value sounds attractive,
but is problematic because there are many options for which giving no value has the same effect as not giving the option at all,
which may have a different meaning. In other words, specifying `-option ""` can mean to return to the default, which is not what we want here.
So using the value `no` would be more clear than providing the empty string.

Meanwhile I've implemented this and will provide the PR when #13614 has been merged,
which cleans up the ground for it (and which I had to extend further).
After all those preparations the generation of default SKID and AKID, to be done here, becomes rather straightforward.

review_comments: I am really not sure the req command needs to duplicate the functionality of x509 command here. IMO the -x509 option for req command should produce self-signed certificates only.

Having the `-CA` and `-CAkey` options not only in the `x509` app but also in the `req` app
makes the two apps more consistent and in particular is very helpful for the test cases I added to `25-test_req.t`.
As I mentioned recently in #13720 there is a large overlap between the `x509`, `req`, and `ca` app,
and the tendency has been to (non always consistently) extend `x509` and `req`,
also with functionality that one would expect for the `ca` app.
Part of the reason must be that `ca` is rather inconvenient to use.
